# Alert tones

`l1.wav`, `l2.wav` and `l3.wav` are the in-drive alert tones for levels L1 (nudge), L2 (warning)
and L3 (urgent). `points_lost.wav` is the cue that follows an alert's tone each time points come
off (alone, for a speeding repeat past its 5-s grace). The four `dp_*.wav` files are the DashPal dashcam's sounds when it routes an alert
to the phone (`src/dashcam/alerts.ts`); a DashPal advisory chime uses `l1.wav`.

**Provenance:** generated by `scripts/make-tones.js` (`npm run tones:make`) from plain sine waves (the wake sound sums odd harmonics).
No third-party or recorded audio is included, so no licence or attribution applies.

| File | Pattern | Length |
|---|---|---|
| `l1.wav` | one soft 880 Hz tone, 20 ms ramps | 180 ms |
| `l2.wav` | 660 Hz then 990 Hz, 150 ms each, back to back | 300 ms |
| `l3.wav` | three pairs of 1040 Hz + 780 Hz (120 ms each), 80 ms between pairs | 880 ms |
| `points_lost.wav` | falling 740 Hz then 494 Hz, 110 ms each, 20 ms apart | 240 ms |
| `dp_glance.wav` | two 1175 Hz pips (90 ms, 60 ms apart), then 880 Hz 140 ms | 440 ms |
| `dp_drowsy.wav` | rising 523 → 659 → 784 Hz (220, 220, 320 ms), 90 ms gaps | 940 ms |
| `dp_wake.wav` | four fast 1500 + 1000 Hz pairs (80 ms each, odd harmonics), 40 ms between pairs | 760 ms |
| `dp_phone.wav` | falling 1320 → 990 → 660 Hz, 120 ms each, back to back | 360 ms |

All are 16-bit mono PCM at 44.1 kHz, peaking at 0.9 of full scale. L1 is soft by its shape, not its
level; any loudness balance between levels is a runtime gain in the alert player. The script is
deterministic: `scripts/__tests__/make-tones.test.ts` fails if these files differ from what it
generates, so edit the script and regenerate rather than editing the audio.
